solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Getting sacked, as I am so inept and fiery

indicators.note: a place that is sacked is ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone explains their dismissal: they were incompetent and hot-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting sacked' reads as losing a job, but it is the signal to rearrange AS I AM SO INEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone full of passionate, burning feeling; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Popular goods available at shop?

parts.note: something popular is said to be in, in fashion
a shop's goods are its stock

explanation.surface: A query about whether popular merchandise can be bought in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that a shop has on its shelves ready to sell are described with this phrase; the question mark admits the loose fit.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, eccentric sees public notice

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a card is an old-fashioned word for an eccentric, amusing person

explanation.surface: An odd character scaling a peak spots a sign posted publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or poster displayed for everyone to read, as at a protest, is a public notice.

clue.text: Full state broadcast ends with a set piece from Shanghai

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order
a piece from the city's name is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A national broadcast closes with a set piece filmed in Shanghai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns ENDS, A and SET into SATEDNES; 'piece from' gives the S of Shanghai to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sated is being completely satisfied with food, so the noun names the condition of being full.

clue.text: Foolish person I spot going around India

indicators.note: the word for spot wraps itself around the letter for India

parts.note: a dot is a small spot
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller sees a fool on a trip around India.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is a stupid person; the two terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Writer knocked up melody for god in the main

indicators.note: in a down entry, knocked up means turned upwards, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A songwriter dashes off a melody honouring a sea god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity ruling the oceans is the god of the sea, the main.

clue.text: Disease left one not-half sick around island capital

indicators.note: the string built from disease, left, one and half of sick goes around the letter for island

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means its first two letters here

explanation.surface: A sick traveller complains of illness picked up around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not-half' keeps the front half of sick; 'around' wraps the whole string about the island letter, which slips in just after the disease. Tbilisi is Georgia's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Georgia, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Heating appliance used in Barnet sport clubs

parts.note: curling is a winter sport played by sliding stones on ice
irons are a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A sports club in Barnet, north London, uses a heater.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough, but it is also Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair).
explanation.definitionFit: These heated tongs are used to put waves into hair, the Barnet of the clue.

clue.text: Arrogant type succeeded in winning pastry dish

indicators.note: the letter for succeeded is placed inside the combination that follows

parts.note: a team that is winning is up
a tart is a pastry dish
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone triumphs by baking a prize-winning tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A presumptuous newcomer who has risen fast and acts self-important is called this.

clue.text: I fibbed about politician, it's insinuated

indicators.note: the words for I fibbed go around the letters for politician

parts.note: to fib is to lie, so fibbed means lied
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A confession of lying about a politician, which suggests something underhand.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest indirectly, so something insinuated is suggested without being said outright.

clue.text: I act with lag messing about with Dutch timepiece

indicators.note: messing about with something means tampering with it, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles with a Dutch clock that runs slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing about' rearranges I ACT WITH LAG into IGITALWATCH, after D for Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch showing the time in numerals rather than with hands is a kind of timepiece.

clue.text: European operation occupying fat cat

indicators.note: the letters for European and operation take up a place inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A European military operation takes over a wealthy fat cat's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' looks like one phrase, but fat is wordplay and cat alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted big cat of Africa and Asia is one example of a cat.

clue.text: University books retro-style band on the road

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters for university and books are reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
a ring is a band, as in a wedding band

explanation.surface: A university hires a nostalgic band for a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A band travelling from venue to venue on tour is said to be on the road.

clue.text: Fife thug steals assault rifle out of habit

indicators.note: the word for the thug takes the rifle into itself, as a thief pockets loot

parts.note: ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan, and Fife is in Scotland
AK is short for the AK-47 Kalashnikov rifle

explanation.surface: A Scottish hoodlum steals a gun, unlike his usual behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of habit' seems to mean out of routine, but a habit is also a garment, as worn by a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of their habit, the robe, is undressed, so wearing nothing.

clue.text: Exit terms to be amended for ultra- Brexiteer?

indicators.note: terms that are amended are changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The UK's withdrawal deal terms get revised to please a hardline Leave supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person holding radical views; one taking Leave to the limit is a radical, the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: One persecuting flipping rubbish teacher

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word for rubbish is read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
a mentor is an adviser or teacher

explanation.surface: A pupil complains about a teacher who is total rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word qualifying rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inflicts suffering or harasses another is a persecutor.

clue.text: One giving out shots? Mine is rum with a twist!

indicators.note: a twisted thing is out of shape, so the letters are wrung into another order

explanation.surface: A barman pours shots, boasting that his rum comes with a twist of lemon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shots' suggests drinks, but here they are injections.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccinator gives jabs, injections, which are informally called shots.

clue.text: President once angry with boy full of ego

indicators.note: the words for angry and boy, side by side, are filled with the letter for ego

parts.note: mad means angry
a son is a boy
ego is Latin for I

explanation.surface: A former president, angry with his conceited son.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States.

clue.text: Some in Washington or Wichita or another city

indicators.note: Some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people live in one American city or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in the second 'or', which only links the hidden text to 'another city'; the first 'or' is part of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk's county town in eastern England is a city, a different one from the two named.

clue.text: Losing foremost of liberals is just terrible

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word for just

parts.note: lawful means just, legitimate

indicators.note: the foremost of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that losing the leading Liberals is simply dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like an adverb, 'simply', but it is the adjective meaning lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean very bad or dreadful; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Messenger with mail tucking into beer

indicators.note: the word for mail is tucked inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
post is mail

explanation.surface: A courier with the mail settles down to a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciples sent out to spread the gospel were messengers; the Greek root means one sent forth.

clue.text: Addicts downing last of cider and Buds

indicators.note: the addicts take the letter down inside them, as if drinking it

parts.note: fiends are addicts, as in dope fiends

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Drinkers knock back cider and Bud lagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buds' reads as Budweiser beers, but it is American slang for pals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bud is informal American for buddy, so buds are pals.

clue.text: Well-organised chap who's a hospital attendant

definitions.meaning: a man employed to do non-medical jobs on hospital wards

explanation.surface: A tidy man works as a hospital porter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means neat and methodical; the noun is a hospital worker who carries out routine tasks.

clue.text: People from America can be jerks

explanation.surface: Americans can be idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' reads as a noun, fools, but it is the verb, tugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for Americans is also a verb for sudden sharp pulls.

clue.text: A Catholic and I ran back to see titillating art

indicators.note: running back means the assembled letters are read from the end

parts.note: tore means ran fast, as in tore down the street

explanation.surface: A Catholic and a friend dash back to look at racy artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature or art meant to arouse sexual desire is titillating art.

clue.text: Leaders to say EU still strong in one new meeting

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Political leaders insist at a new summit that the EU is still strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like heads of state; it takes the first letter of each word from say to new.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting of a court, council or group is a meeting of that body.

clue.text: Huge singer seen by a French resort briefly

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, so a singer

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A massive pop star is spotted on a brief trip to a French resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, from the Titans of Greek myth.

clue.text: Honest setter sadly could become homeless

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A truthful crossword compiler might end up homeless, given the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no home, sleeping rough outdoors, is said to be living on the streets.
